subject: Stitch-Up proposal — hybrid retrieval pattern (pgvector + S3) for Albedo
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@pinecone.io>, Sam Park <sam@atlasdata.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Stitch-Up proposal — hybrid retrieval pattern (pgvector + S3) for Albedo

Hi Alex / Sam / team,

Following our call last week, attached is a short proposal for a "Stitch-Up" integration that lets Albedo route first to a low-latency pgvector index for hot docs and fall back to S3-based cold retrieval + on-demand rehydration when the index miss rate exceeds their budget. High-level goals:

- Preserve 95th-percentile QPS latency under 250ms for common queries.
- Limit cold hits to <5% of calls via prefix caching and short-lived KV warmups.
- Keep embedding storage costs predictable by charging cold rehydrates separately.

Attachments: stitch-up-proposal.pdf (technical flow + API contract), latency-cost-matrix.xlsx (cost model for sample workload).

Open questions for partners:
- Can Pinecone support a light-weight marker or metadata flag on vector items to indicate cold-resident objects that should trigger S3 rehydrate?
- What operational signal would you recommend for automatic reindexing (time-based TTL vs write-driven)?
- Commercially, do you prefer a per-rehydrate fee or a revenue-share pilot for the first 90 days?

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical sync (30–45m) w/ engineering owners to walk the flow and clarify API hooks.
2) Mutual action plan with milestone-based pilot (60–90 days).
3) Procurement touchpoint to align on partner term sheet and PO path.

Connor / Ben / Vanessa — could you review the latency/cost spreadsheet and note any red flags by EOD Tuesday? Alex / Sam — can you confirm if Pinecone has a metadata hook we can use, or if a little proxy layer is required?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Partner Integrations — Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stitch-Up proposal — hybrid retrieval pattern (pgvector + S3) for Albedo

Neha — quick notes after skimming the sheet:

- Index freshness: If Albedo's update cadence is high (many small writes), TTL-driven reindex will generate a lot of churn. We should prefer a write-driven marker where writes set a "cold=false" tag. That avoids periodic full scans.
- Warmup window: Recommend a tiny in-memory hot-cache (kv-cache) for 1–2 minutes after an S3 rehydrate to catch repeat queries; this would drastically cut rehydrate costs.
- Consistency model: We need to be explicit whether the rehydrated document is treated as the source-of-truth or if eventual reconciliation is acceptable for their use-case.

I put inline comments in latency-cost-matrix.xlsx about assumptions and a rough ballpark for rehydrate cost per 1k requests. If Pinecone can surface a metadata flag on fetch, we can avoid the proxy layer I mentioned.

Ben
Principal SWE — Indexing & Runtime
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Stitch-Up proposal — hybrid retrieval pattern (pgvector + S3) for Albedo

Thanks Neha & team — appreciate the clear summary. A few notes from Pinecone's side:

1) Metadata hook: We don't currently expose an explicit "cold" marker on fetch that triggers partner-side rehydrate, but we can add a small boolean in the fetch response (on our partner API) within a two-week engineering window. That would let Redwood handle rehydrate logic without a proxy.

2) Reindexing: We agree with Ben — write-driven markers are preferable. We can emit a write webhook to your ingestion endpoint so you can invalidate/refresh the S3->index mapping as updates arrive.

3) Pilot commercial: We'd propose a 90-day trial with the following options: a) flat per-rehydrate unit fee ($0.01 / rehydrate) for the pilot; or b) 70/30 revenue share on rehydrate billings if Redwood is billing the end customer for cold hits. We're open to whichever simplifies procurement for Albedo. The term-sheet attached contains both options.

4) Ops & SLA: We'll commit a 99.5% read availability for the vector tier during pilot and provide a monthly latency report.

I've attached a brief partner-term-sheet.pdf and uploaded a starter DocuSign envelope for the pilot terms: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/SAMPLE-123456789. Also shared a quick runbook in the partner portal: https://partners.pinecone.io/portal/partner-stitchup (internal link).

Happy to join a technical sync next week — I can bring a PM and an engineer to walk the webhook and response flags.

—Alex
Alex Rivera

- Procurement (procurement@albedo.com): please review the partner-term-sheet.pdf and the DocuSign envelope linked here: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/SAMPLE-123456789. If you want a PO, loop us in and we will route to Redwood finance.

If nobody objects, we'll run the pilot under the per-rehydrate pilot fee and re-evaluate after 60 days.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting a lightweight pilot running.
